steps.stopIfMissing: Do not publish a green run while the artifact directory contains unowned files, an expected artifact is missing, metadata is stale, or the failure phase is ambiguous.

steps.action: Label whether evidence came from deterministic non-render assertions, a Fabric Client GameTest client under a virtual framebuffer, or an interactive client environment. A virtual-framebuffer run can exercise an actual client render-and-capture path in that declared environment, but it does not prove physical display, GPU and driver, window-manager, native input, accessibility, shader, or complete installed-extension-set behavior. Non-client headless assertions prove no rendered pixels. Interactive-client evidence is still specific to its recorded environment. Verify every concrete test entrypoint, screenshot, wait, and Loom configuration name against current official Fabric documentation and target-version Fabric API or mapping documentation instead of presenting one API spelling as universal.
evidence: An environment class and recorded client, operating system, display, renderer, hardware or software graphics, window, GUI scale, locale, and relevant client-extension metadata
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/automatic-testing
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/loom/fabric-api
Target-version Fabric API Javadocs or selected mappings for every concrete client-test API named by an implementation
A limitations statement distinguishing non-render assertions, virtual-framebuffer client evidence, and interactive-client evidence
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not describe non-client assertions as rendered evidence, virtual-framebuffer results as hardware or interaction proof, or target-specific Fabric API names as universal.

recipes.failureMode: Screenshots can look authoritative while unstable case identity, early capture, partial selection, silent baseline replacement, stale artifacts, or an overstated headless environment makes the evidence incomplete or irreproducible.

recipes.title: Design Fabric client UI without double scaling or hidden clipping
when: The task creates or reviews a Fabric client screen, overlay, widget, or custom UI layout.
Text, images, controls, or input regions clip, shift, shrink, or stop aligning when GUI scale, window size, language, or interaction state changes.
The UI needs repeatable geometry and rendered evidence across multiple client display conditions.

steps.action: Read the target-version screen or window values that already represent the current scaled viewport and establish them as the layout coordinate space. Capture configured GUI scale, resolved scale, window and framebuffer dimensions, and scaled viewport dimensions as one case tuple. Treat Auto as a runtime-resolved family of tuples, not as one magic scale value. Do not apply GUI scale again to layout, draw, clip, or pointer coordinates.
evidence: A coordinate-space table for viewport, framebuffer, draw, clip, and input values
Captured case tuples including configured GUI scale, resolved scale, window dimensions, framebuffer dimensions, and scaled viewport dimensions
Current official Fabric documentation and target-version mappings for concrete Screen and window APIs
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not compensate for uncertain coordinates with another scale multiplication or division; verify the target-version scaled viewport and input surfaces first.

steps.action: Compute an immutable layout result from the scaled viewport, content measurements, and interaction state. Include component bounds, pre-clip content bounds, child placement, local clip, parent clip, effective ancestor intersection, and hit-test or focus bounds. Consume this same result for rendering, clip setup, and input instead of rebuilding related rectangles in separate paths.
evidence: One layout-result type or fixture containing every render, clip, child, and hit-test rectangle
Assertions that component and ancestor clips form the effective intersection
Assertions that render and input paths consume the same state-specific layout result
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not approve separately calculated draw, scissor, and pointer bounds whose equality is only assumed.

steps.action: Measure complete glyph and image bounds before applying clips. Compare those bounds with the component, parent, and effective clip. If content intentionally exceeds a boundary, select and test an explicit wrapping, scrolling, ellipsis, crop, or overflow policy; clipped output alone must not turn accidental overflow into a passing result. Keep nested clip ownership balanced on every render path.
evidence: Pre-clip glyph and image rectangles
Component, parent, and effective clip comparisons
An explicit and tested overflow policy for every intentionally non-fitting content path
Balanced nested clip setup and teardown across normal and exceptional render paths
steps.stopIfMissing: A clean post-clip screenshot is not evidence that full content bounds fit or that nested clips are balanced.

steps.action: Define a deterministic case matrix with the minimum supported scaled viewport, long localized translations, multiple resolved scales, Auto at more than one window size, and normal, hover, pressed, and disabled states. Assert layout bounds, pre-clip content, clip intersections, and hit regions for every case. Then capture actual client renders or screenshots for the same matrix so visual artifacts supplement rather than replace geometry proof.
evidence: Parameterized geometry tests for every viewport, scale, Auto, translation, and interaction-state case
Numeric assertions for layout, pre-clip content, effective clips, and hit-test bounds
Actual-render or screenshot artifacts labeled with the same case tuples
A review result that distinguishes deterministic geometry failures from visual-rendering failures
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not claim scale or clipping safety from the default language, one large viewport, one GUI scale, one interaction state, or screenshots alone.

steps.action: Consult current official Fabric custom-screen and GUI-rendering documentation plus target-version mappings to verify every concrete Screen, window, drawing, input, and scissor API named by the implementation. Keep unverified details out of generated code and present the coordinate, layout, and test rules as general design guidance when exact APIs are unavailable.
evidence: https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/rendering/gui/custom-screens
https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/rendering/gui-graphics
Target-version Fabric Yarn or other selected mapping documentation for each named Minecraft API
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not convert general UI geometry guidance into target-version API claims without current official documentation and mapping evidence.

recipes.failureMode: Independent scale, render, clip, and input calculations can pass a single screenshot while producing clipped content or misaligned controls in other resolved viewport cases.

recipes.title: Generate or review bounded Paper world operations across chunk boundaries
when: the request loads, generates, pins, scans, or mutates multiple chunks from a Paper or Bukkit plugin
block edits, drops, entity movement or removal, or teleportation can cross a chunk, tick, unload, or Folia region boundary
the implementation uses async chunk loading, plugin chunk tickets, repeated world batches, RegionScheduler, EntityScheduler, or chunk lifecycle events
the review must prevent tick-thread blocking, stale references, ticket leaks, duplicate partial side effects, or shutdown races

steps.action: Resolve the target Paper version and verify the exact World, Chunk, Block, Entity, teleport, RegionScheduler, EntityScheduler, and event APIs from official Paper sources. Convert the complete requested selection into deduplicated world-and-chunk coordinates, define generation allowed or forbidden, and reject unknown, unbounded, or over-limit work before loading or mutation begins.
evidence: Target-version Javadocs matches for every overload and callback or completion context used
A bounded target manifest containing world identities, chunk coordinates, generation policy, maximum chunks, maximum targets, timeout, and rejection rules
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not begin loading or mutation until the complete chunk set, generation policy, target-version APIs, and hard limits are known.

steps.action: Acquire only the bounded target chunks through target-version-supported asynchronous APIs. Never wait or block via Future.get or Future.join on a server main, tick, or region thread. Treat isChunkLoaded as a snapshot, and if residency is required, let one lifecycle owner track exact plugin-ticket claims, shared references, deadlines, and release responsibility.
evidence: Target-version evidence for async chunk acquisition, generation flags, callback or Future completion context, isChunkLoaded, and plugin-ticket add and remove behavior
A bounded acquisition queue and ticket ledger that distinguishes claims added by this operation from same-plugin shared residency
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not synchronously wait on chunk acquisition or treat a loaded snapshot as a lease; reject the design until asynchronous continuation and owned residency are explicit.

steps.action: Never dereference a retained world target outside its verified owner or treat it as current after lifecycle changes without owner-local revalidation. Carry immutable world identity plus coordinates for block and location work, then re-resolve and validate them on the owning region. For entity work, use that entity's scheduler as the handoff mechanism and validate the entity's identity, validity, lifecycle state, operation generation, plugin state, and preconditions inside the owned callback instead of requiring a cross-region World.getEntity lookup. Keep EntityScheduler retired callbacks minimal: record or forward terminal intent only, then perform entity, chunk, world, or ticket cleanup in a verified safe context.
evidence: A scheduler-ownership map for Paper and any claimed Folia support

Tests proving retained Chunk, Block, BlockState, mutable Location, and Entity values are never dereferenced outside their verified owner or treated as current after lifecycle changes without owner-local revalidation
An entity-scheduler handoff that revalidates the entity inside the owned callback without requiring cross-region World.getEntity lookup, plus a location-region path for block and location mutation
A retired or scheduling-failure path whose critical retired callback only records or forwards minimal terminal intent and defers entity, chunk, world, and ticket-level cleanup
steps.stopIfMissing: Async completion is not mutation ownership; do not touch block or location state until it is re-resolved in its owning region, or entity state until the entity-scheduler callback revalidates it.

steps.action: Process a fixed maximum of targets and elapsed work per tick and per region, recording a resumable cursor and bounded diagnostics. Stop when cancelled, timed out, stale, unloaded, or disabled, and emit complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, or unloaded with attempted, applied, skipped, failed, and remaining counts.
evidence: Explicit item and time budgets for each tick and region plus an upper bound on queued callbacks and diagnostics
Typed progress and terminal outcomes that do not equate Future or callback completion with full mutation success
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not run an unbounded chunk, block, drop, or entity loop in one callback or report unconditional success without per-target progress.

steps.action: Before every side effect and resumed batch, recheck assumptions affected by neighboring physics, drops, entity movement or removal, teleport completion, chunk unload, cancellation, and plugin disable. Inspect teleport Boolean results, treat entity retirement or unload separately from death or despawn, and never use applyPhysics=false as a general safety or persistence guarantee.
evidence: Target-version Paper Javadocs for block physics flags, teleport results, entity scheduler retirement, and chunk or entity lifecycle events used
Race tests in which physics changes neighbors, a dropped or moved entity disappears, teleport returns false, a chunk unloads, or plugin disable begins between acquisition and apply
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not infer a final world state from scheduling, event delivery, applyPhysics=false, an unloaded entity, or a completed teleport Future; inspect the actual result and current target.

steps.action: Give the operation a stable identity and record per-target compare-before-apply progress. On retry or recovery, reconcile observed postconditions and resume only unapplied work so drops, entity removals, teleports, and other non-idempotent effects cannot repeat after partial completion.
evidence: A per-target progress model and compare-before-apply rule
Tests that interrupt after partial mutation and prove retries neither repeat committed side effects nor skip remaining work
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not retry a partially applied world operation until committed effects can be distinguished from remaining work.

steps.action: Use one lifecycle owner to accept exactly one terminal transition, stop new work, reconcile committed effects, settle the typed outcome, and release every owned ticket or scheduled resource once. Cover complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, unloaded, cancellation, exception, and plugin disable independently of whether lifecycle events arrive.
evidence: A ticket ledger and terminal-state transition that release only owned claims and handle shared same-plugin residency
Assertions that every terminal and plugin-disable path leaves no operation-owned tickets, batches, or unresolved completion
Tests proving duplicate events, callbacks, cancellation, and shutdown cleanup are idempotent
steps.stopIfMissing: Do not rely on automatic ticket release or events alone; the lifecycle owner must independently release every owned claim exactly once.

recipes.failureMode: A cross-chunk operation can block the owning tick, pin unbounded chunks, cross scheduler ownership, reuse unloaded targets, repeat partial side effects, or leak resources unless target discovery, acquisition, batches, outcomes, reconciliation, and cleanup share one bounded lifecycle.
